cases.prompt: A print shop has 84 blank labels. It prints 3 batches of 17 labels and sets aside 12 still-blank labels for tomorrow. How many blank labels remain available for another batch today?
cases.answerInstructions: Give the number and a concise calculation. State any assumption that matters.

candidateClaims.text: The number available today is 21.
The 12 labels set aside count as available for another batch today.

cases.prompt: A class has 8 students who each scored 12 points and 24 students who each scored 20 points. What is the class mean score?
cases.answerInstructions: Give the mean and a concise calculation.

candidateClaims.text: The mean score is 18.
Averaging 12 and 20 without weighting gives the class mean.

cases.prompt: A subscription costs 250 credits. Its price is reduced by 20%, then the reduced price is increased by 20%. What is the final price, and how does it compare with the original?
cases.answerInstructions: Give the final price and percentage difference from the original.

candidateClaims.text: The final price is 240 credits.
Equal percentage decreases and increases cancel exactly.
The final price is 4% below the original.

cases.prompt: Four workshops—J, K, L, and M—occupy slots 1 through 4, one per slot. J is before K. L is immediately after J. M is not in slot 4. Which schedule is possible?
cases.answerInstructions: Select one option and briefly check every constraint.

candidateClaims.text: Option B satisfies every stated constraint.
Option D satisfies every stated constraint.

cases.prompt: A wellness course enrolled 60 volunteers. Seven withdrew before the final survey. Of the 53 who completed it, 41 reported better sleep. There was no control group and sleep was self-reported. What can the study support?
cases.answerInstructions: State the supported descriptive result and whether the course caused better sleep.

candidateClaims.text: 41 of 53 completers reported better sleep.
The course caused better sleep for the enrolled volunteers.
The seven withdrawals create a possible attrition concern.

evidence.text: Enrollment: 60; withdrawals: 7; completers reporting better sleep: 41; no control group; self-reported outcome.

cases.prompt: A January policy note says reimbursements require receipts from April onward. A March amendment says: 'The receipt requirement begins May 1 and replaces the January start date.' When does the requirement begin?
cases.answerInstructions: Give the operative date and cite the supplied sentence that controls.

candidateClaims.text: The receipt requirement begins April 1.
The receipt requirement begins May 1.
The March amendment supersedes the January start date.

evidence.text: January note: receipts required from April onward.
March amendment: The receipt requirement begins May 1 and replaces the January start date.

cases.prompt: A cafe installed a sidewalk sign on Friday. Weekend sales were 30% higher than the previous weekend. A street festival also took place that weekend, and no comparable cafe without a sign was observed. What causal conclusion is justified?
cases.answerInstructions: Separate the observed association from any causal claim and name the material alternative explanation.

candidateClaims.text: Weekend sales were 30% higher after the sign was installed.
The sign caused the entire sales increase.
The festival is a material alternative explanation.

evidence.text: Sign installed Friday; sales rose 30% versus the prior weekend; a street festival occurred; no comparison cafe was observed.

cases.prompt: A quarterly note states: 'Revenue was 120 in Q1 and 150 in Q2. Expenses were 80 in Q1 and 95 in Q2.' By how much did operating surplus (revenue minus expenses) change?
cases.answerInstructions: Give both surpluses and the change. Report no issue if the supplied figures suffice.

candidateClaims.text: Operating surplus was 40 in Q1.
Operating surplus was 55 in Q2.
Operating surplus increased by 15.

evidence.text: Q1 revenue 120 and expenses 80; Q2 revenue 150 and expenses 95.

cases.prompt: Rina told Maya that she had been selected for the fellowship. Who was selected?
cases.answerInstructions: Answer only as specifically as the sentence permits. Ask one clarification if needed.

candidateClaims.text: Rina was selected.
Maya was selected.
The pronoun makes the selected person ambiguous.

cases.prompt: Please move the weekly planning meeting to Thursday afternoon. Will this work?
cases.answerInstructions: Identify what is missing before claiming the move works, and ask the smallest useful question.

candidateClaims.text: Thursday afternoon definitely works for everyone.
The desired time, time zone, attendees, and their availability are not specified.
The user should supply or confirm the scheduling constraints.

cases.prompt: A courier charges 9 credits for parcels up to 2 kg and 14 credits for parcels over 2 kg. What will it cost to send my parcel?
cases.answerInstructions: Answer without guessing. State the missing fact and the consequence of each possible value.

candidateClaims.text: The charge is definitely 9 credits.
The parcel's weight is required to choose the price.
At exactly 2 kg the charge is 9 credits; above 2 kg it is 14.

evidence.text: Up to and including 2 kg: 9 credits. Over 2 kg: 14 credits.

cases.prompt: Every cedar in the garden is a tree. This plant is a tree. Must this plant be a cedar?
cases.answerInstructions: Answer yes or no and identify the logical assumption behind the tempting contrary answer.

candidateClaims.text: The plant must be a cedar.
Being a tree is sufficient to establish that a plant is a cedar.
The conclusion does not follow from the premise.

cases.prompt: Vendor North costs 10,000 credits per year and reports 99.5% historical uptime. Vendor South costs 7,000 and reports 98.5% historical uptime. No outage-cost estimate, switching cost, contract detail, or measurement audit is supplied. Which vendor should we choose?
cases.answerInstructions: Preserve defensible alternatives and identify the decision cruxes instead of inventing a single winner.

candidateClaims.text: Vendor North is unconditionally the correct choice.
Vendor South is unconditionally the correct choice.
Either choice can be defensible depending on outage cost, risk tolerance, and contract quality.

evidence.text: North: 10,000/year, reported 99.5% uptime. South: 7,000/year, reported 98.5% uptime. Other decision inputs are absent.

cases.prompt: A community group can hold one meeting. Option A is a weekday evening with live captions. Option B is a weekend afternoon with on-site childcare. The group has not asked members which barrier affects them. Which option is fairer?
cases.answerInstructions: Name the distinct access benefits, preserve the unresolved tradeoff, and ask the people affected for the missing information.

candidateClaims.text: Option A is inherently fairer for every member.
Option B is inherently fairer for every member.
The fairness judgment depends on affected members' access needs and preferences.

cases.prompt: A team has one spare week. Plan A spends it improving reliability for current users. Plan B spends it prototyping a requested new feature. Both fit the week; expected impact and strategic priority are unknown. Which plan is better?
cases.answerInstructions: Give conditional recommendations and the smallest user-owned question that would decide between them.

candidateClaims.text: Plan A is always better than Plan B.
Plan B is always better than Plan A.
The choice depends on the team's current objective and evidence about expected impact.

cases.prompt: Apartment A costs 900 credits monthly and adds 50 minutes of commuting per day. Apartment B costs 1,150 and adds 10 minutes. Both meet the stated housing requirements. Which should I rent?
cases.answerInstructions: Do not choose the user's value tradeoff. Quantify the known difference and ask for the missing preference or constraint.

candidateClaims.text: Apartment A is necessarily better because it is cheaper.
Apartment B is necessarily better because it saves commute time.
The decision trades 250 credits per month against 40 minutes of commuting per day.
